sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Unzip and place instruction files
sections.what: Checks out the repository, unzips the build kit, copies the two instruction files to the top, sets up .claude and mirrors it to .agent, and sorts the docs into their folder.
sections.why: Likely reason: the agents read those instruction files from the top level, so they must sit there.
sections.watch_out: The docs sort matches only certain file names. Other docs are skipped without warning.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Folders, sync script, ignore list and push
sections.what: Creates the empty project folders, writes the sync script and the ignore list, prints the final tree, then commits and pushes everything.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets up the standard folders before the first commit.
sections.watch_out: Because everything is staged, check the commit log before trusting that no private files were included.

summary: One-time GitHub Actions job that unpacks a build kit, sets up the project's folders and instruction files, then commits and pushes them.
purpose: Creates the starting layout of the CareerOS repository.
why: Likely reason: it was written for a one-time setup from uploaded zip files. Reason for the commit identity not stated in the code.
how: 1. Runs only when started by hand. 2. Unzips the build kit files if present. 3. Copies CLAUDE.md and DATA_CONTRACT.md to the top, using placeholders if missing. 4. Creates the .claude and .agent folders. 5. Sorts the docs into docs/build-kit. 6. Creates the empty folder structure. 7. Writes the sync script and the ignore list. 8. Commits everything and pushes.
inputs: The uploaded zip files in the repository (CareerOS-BuildKit.zip and files.zip) and the GitHub token.
outputs: New folders and files, a sync script, an ignore list, and a pushed commit.
risks: It stages everything with git add -A, so any file not covered by the ignore list gets pushed. The workflow has write permission on the repository. The placeholder text uses doubled backslash escapes, so placeholder files may contain a literal backslash-n instead of a line break. The commit identity uses a made-up address.
debug: If files are missing, read the file lists printed by the find steps in the log. If the push fails, check the token's write permission. If docs are missing, check the file name patterns in the sort step.
